As she tells it, Catherine Roberts dreamed her son Nat, deployed to Iraq, was wrapped in a quilt. She woke up in her Delaware sewing room and made one, then sent it to a wounded stranger at Walter Reed. Volunteers have since hand-sewn over 454,000 Quilts of Valor for veterans touched by war, about 3,000 a month. The 450,000th went out in July 2026. They are still sewing. - Fun Facts

Patsy Ann was a bull terrier, deaf from birth. She still knew which Juneau dock a ship would use, long before it came into sight. In 1934, Juneau's mayor named her the city's official greeter. One day a newspaper printed the wrong dock. The crowd gathered there, but Patsy Ann walked to the correct one instead. The ship proved her right. Her bronze statue still greets every cruise ship today. - Fun Facts

Hugh Laurie played TV's Dr. House for eight years. Off camera, he was chasing something real: a life as a blues musician. He recruited New Orleans legends Dr. John and Irma Thomas for his debut album, Let Them Talk. It hit No. 1 on Billboard's Blues Albums chart. Two years later, his follow-up, Didn't It Rain, did it again. The TV doctor now has two No. 1 blues albums. - Fun Facts

Hibbing is an old mining town on Minnesota's Iron Range. In 1919, the mining company found its ore ran directly under the town. So it moved the entire town two miles south. Workers rolled nearly 200 buildings there on logs and steel rails. One hotel didn't survive the trip. The empty ground became a pit long billed as the world's largest open-pit iron mine. Hibbing still stands today, two miles from where it started. - Fun Facts

Jalen Hurts kept hearing the same story. Philadelphia schools were sending kids home early because classrooms were too hot. So the Eagles quarterback paid to install air conditioning in ten schools himself. More than 300 units later, over 5,000 students and staff have cool classrooms. Now every touchdown he scores pays for more. - Fun Facts

Jesse Cole sold one season ticket in his first two months running the Savannah Bananas. He sold his house and slept on an air mattress in a duplex. One night a cockroach crawled across his face. Locals said he'd never sell another ticket. The opener sold out anyway. The team says every home game has since. This summer that meant an NFL stadium. Every game still sells out. - Fun Facts

George Washington's army was pinned against the East River on the night of August 29, 1776, two days after losing the Battle of Long Island. Washington ordered a silent evacuation. Colonel John Glover's Marblehead fishermen rowed 9,000 soldiers across, boat after boat. Near dawn, a thick fog hid the last crossings. Washington left on the final boat. The British woke up to empty trenches. - Fun Facts

Sturgis, South Dakota has 7,000 residents and hosts the world's biggest motorcycle rally, which drew a record 739,000 riders in 2015. It began in 1938 with nine riders racing for a crowd under 200. Pappy Hoel had just opened an Indian Motorcycle shop and formed the Jackpine Gypsies. His wife Pearl counted the bikes the night before and cooked a picnic for every rider. She kept doing it until the 1950s, when the crowd outgrew her kitchen. - Fun Facts

The Goodyear Blimp has floated over college football since the 1955 Rose Bowl. Over the 64 years that followed, it covered more than 2,000 games. In January 2019, the College Football Hall of Fame gave it an honorary induction. More than 1,300 people are enshrined there. The blimp is still the only member who isn't human. Fans still watch the sky to see if a game is a big one. - Fun Facts

Big Tex is the 55-foot cowboy who greets everyone at the State Fair of Texas. He wasn't always a cowboy. In 1949, tiny Kerens, Texas, built a 49-foot Santa Claus to save its Christmas shopping season. Dallas bought him in 1951 and turned him into a cowboy. He debuted in 1952 wearing size-70 boots and a 75-gallon hat. He's greeted fairgoers with "Howdy, folks!" since 1953. - Fun Facts

Reveille, Texas A&M's collie mascot, outranks every cadet on campus. She holds the rank of Cadet General, with five diamonds - the Corps Commander only wears four. It started in 1931, when cadets hit a stray dog near Navasota and hid her in the dorm. She barked at the bugler's reveille call the next morning, and the name stuck. The rule stands: if she falls asleep on a cadet's bed, that cadet sleeps on the floor. - Fun Facts

USCGC Eagle led America's 250th birthday parade through New York Harbor on July 4, 2026. The three-masted tall ship started life in 1936 as the Horst Wessel, training future officers for Hitler's navy. The US took her in 1946 as compensation after World War II. Nearly every Coast Guard Academy graduate since has trained aboard the same ship. - Fun Facts
